title: The Power of Appreciation or Not
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece makes the claim that people default to assuming they are undervalued unless a leader explicitly tells them otherwise, even when they're already highly rewarded and included. The author explains this through a need for ongoing validation in the face of uncertainty and ambiguity, arguing that showing appreciation through actions alone isn't sufficient — it has to be said out loud. The piece supplies several sample phrases leaders can use and closes with a Voltaire quote about appreciation as reciprocal.
points: People will assume they are undervalued by default unless a leader explicitly says otherwise, regardless of how well they're already treated.
Uncertainty and ambiguity heighten the human need for ongoing validation from people whose opinion carries authority or status.
Showing appreciation through actions and rewards alone isn't enough — leaders need to say it out loud in words as well.
The piece supplies concrete sample phrases leaders can use to voice appreciation directly rather than assuming it's understood.
quotes: If people aren’t told or shown that they are appreciated and valued, they will presume the opposite.
Unless a leader explicitly tells people they are appreciated, over time they will come to feel undervalued and taken for granted.
In a world of profound uncertainty, overt ambiguity, competitive jealousy, and constant change, people seek validation.
Appreciation is an echo from the lips of leaders to the walls of great teams.
Appreciation is a wonderful thing: It makes what is excellent in others belong to us as well.
